title: Radio: Boom Team 4, Mile 31 Deflection Failed

fields.orgName: Ironbark Pipeline Company / Kansas River Unified Command
fields.centerName: Incident Command Post, Mill Ridge Station (MP 213.1)

lines.text: Command, Prairie Spill Field Lead. Boom Team 4 is on the two-hour check. The mile 31 deflection station has failed. The stakes on the upstream two sections pulled out of the sand overnight. About 800 feet has swung square to the current and is trailing. Oil is going under it.
Field Lead, Command. Copy, mile 31 failed and oil going under. Where's it headed?

Fresh brown sheen, maybe 30 feet wide, moving down the left bank toward the mile 33 station and the Sterling Bluff exclusion boom. At this current that's under an hour to 33. Second thing. The morning flow is flushing Cottonwood Slough at mile 22. Oil we had trapped behind the exclusion boom is coming out around the downstream end in streamers.

Boom. The only spare 18-inch is at the Wichita depot, 1,500 feet of it. They're loading now, and with three and a half hours on the road that's about 12:30 here, not sooner. Topeka and Kansas City have 400 feet each left and no crews free to move it. I can pull 400 feet off mile 9.5 right now if you'll release it. I need a yes or no.

All stations, Planning. Status board update. The last trajectory posted is TRJ-02, model run 07:45 yesterday, and the 11:45 rerun it called for was never posted. We have no current trajectory for a re-release from mile 22 or mile 31. Do not use TRJ-02 windows for mile 33 or mile 34.

fields.voiceStyle: Field lead: man in his forties, outdoors on a riverbank, steady but clipped, a little winded. Command: calm, flat. Environmental Unit: woman, measured and precise.

instructorNote: This is a technical hurdle. It re-opens a threat to Sterling Bluff just as players start talking about reopening. The OSRO should re-angle the surviving sections to about 15° and re-anchor them with sandbags, ask UC to release the 400 ft from mile 9.5 now, and give an realistic Wichita ETA. The ENVL should have TRJ-03 re-run by NOAA's support coordinator with a new run time and windows for mile 33/34 and update the ICS 232. The QI should add the re-release to the ICS 202 and tell the Sterling Bluff and RWD operators directly. Watch for anyone who reads this as a reason to un-stake boom square across the flow, or to treat yesterday's TRJ-02 windows as current.
